title: Full-Continuum Ultrafast Quantum Gas Microscopy
authors: Andrea Litvinov, Clemens Ulm, Eva Casotti, Gerard Solà Berga, Manfred J. Mark, Francesca Ferlaino
abstract: Quantum gas microscopy provides single-shot access to many-body configurations, but their microscopic reconstruction has so far largely relied on a predefined discrete spatial basis during fluorescence readout. Here we realize ultrafast atom-resolved fluorescence microscopy of an ultracold $^{162}$Dy gas directly in continuous space, with all external confinement removed during imaging. Exploiting the large mass and broad optical transition of dysprosium together with a high numerical aperture in-vacuum objective, we detect single atoms within $4\,μ\mathrm{s}$ while maintaining an effective point-spread function with a full width at half maximum of $254.8(3)\,\mathrm{nm}$, and an isolated single-atom classification fidelity of $99.72(3)\%$. We use the measured single-atom response to construct a statistical configuration-inference model that recovers atomic positions and multiplicities, coming from overlapping atoms, directly from single fluorescence snapshots. Benchmarking our model on Monte-Carlo generated images shows a total reconstruction fidelity of $98.7\%$. Our approach extends quantum gas microscopy beyond predefined detection lattices, enabling atom-resolved measurements of counting statistics and higher-order spatial correlations directly on the intrinsic length scales of continuum many-body systems.
summary: This paper presents an advanced quantum gas microscopy technique that achieves atom-resolved imaging of ultracold atoms directly in continuous space, bypassing the need for confining lattices. By developing a statistical inference model, the authors can reconstruct the true atomic positions and density correlations from raw fluorescence photon counts, enabling measurements on the intrinsic length scales of quantum gases.
main_problem: To overcome the limitation of relying on predefined discrete spatial bases for quantum gas microscopy, the authors developed a method for ultrafast, atom-resolved imaging directly in continuous space.
main_result: The technique successfully images atoms at sub-micrometre separations in free space, and a statistical inference model achieves a high reconstruction fidelity of 98.7% on simulated data.
method: The method combines ultrafast fluorescence microscopy with a statistical configuration-inference model that reconstructs atomic positions and multiplicities from raw photon count data.
model_or_system: The system utilizes an ultracold dysprosium gas imaged via fluorescence microscopy. The reconstruction relies on modeling the measured photon count probability distribution as a convolution of noise and Poissonian single-emitter contributions.
key_observables: Single-atom classification fidelity (99.72%), effective Point-Spread Function (PSF) FWHM (254.8 nm), and total reconstruction fidelity (98.7%).
important_parameters: Imaging time scale ($	au$) of $4\ \mu	ext{s}$, and the ability to operate beyond predefined detection lattices.
main_assumptions: The statistical inference assumes conditional independence of ring kernels when calculating the joint likelihood of the atomic configuration.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the in-vacuum microscope setup, single-shot fluorescence images of BECs and thermal gases, and detailed characterizations of the PSF scaling ($	au^{3/2}$) and photon-count statistics.
paper_structure: The paper details the experimental setup for continuous-space imaging, characterizes the single-atom response and PSF, develops the statistical framework using probability distributions and characteristic functions, and finally applies this framework to reconstruct atomic configurations from measured photon counts.
why_interesting: This work pushes the boundaries of quantum gas imaging by providing a robust, lattice-free method to measure intrinsic many-body correlations, which is crucial for studying continuum physics in ultracold atomic systems.

Atoms are loaded in a single plane of a vertical accordion lattice with 3 µm spac- ing, whose phase is controlled by rotating a phase plate. The vertical lattice provides a band gap exceeding h×3 kHz, corre- sponding to a harmonic-oscillator length aho < 150 nm, while the in-plane trap frequencies remain between 5 and 50 Hz.
